text_fidelity_a:
Fire TV Stick 4K streaming device with Alexa Voice Remote (includes TV controls) | Dolby Vision I have one on each of the TVs in my RV and in my home. I stream almost everything now because Fire stick make it so easy. With Prime, there are so many great things to watch and the music options are outstanding. Even YouTube videos play great with this device. All the premium channels can be used with a subscription. There are also at least 3 very good free streaming services that can be added even if you don't subscribe to Prime Video. And it remembers your log ins to multiple sites so you only need to log in once and after that, it's automatic!

The voice command feature is a real advantage. It's very high quality and is far more accurate than my typing. The volume control addition is a great improvement, too. And it can function on weak connections over shared WIFI signals. I can't think of anything to complain of... Turning my TVs into streaming devices simplifies so many things. I just love it.
text_fidelity_b: Fire TV Stick 4K streaming device with Alexa Voice Remote (includes TV controls) | Dolby Vision

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version) I have had these for a day. They are absolutely amazing. Life changing, worth every penny. I have seen a lot of reviews where they were compared to AirPods Pros, but there is no comparison.

I bought them because I have a noisy (but lovable) neighbor. The noise cancellation on these is superior, but not for low, bassy, external sounds, but rather sounds in the higher range.

My advise, and to save you some time: Do not get the app. It is so invasive of your information, and I know all apps are, but this one is probably the worst. You can set up bluetooth with all your devices without the app, and use all the features, no problem.

It also has Alexa built in, which is insane, I have yet to pull the trigger on giving Alexa permission, but I think I will; there is an Alexa button, I THINK that's the only time it's listening. If you're like me, and you have Amazon Prime Music the combo is insane.

A few cons: the Noise Cancellation will pound your ears if you’re not listening to content. I didn’t know it could do this, but I can see why people say they can only wear them for so long.

Do not under any circumstance get the app. It’s much more invasive than any app I’ve seen (of tkunborher to read the privacy (publicity) statement. Your earphones can operate fine without the app.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WH1000XM3 Noise Cancelling Headphones, Wireless Bluetooth Over the Ear Headset – Black (2018 Version)

text_fidelity_a:
TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions This GPS is a real upgrade for me, but I still love my old one which is TomTom One. Too bad it's no longer supported by TomTom or I probably would not have chosen the TomTom Via 1525 to try out for review. The very first thing I noticed about it was that the screen was twice as large as on my One - a very coveted perk to me. I choose to still use separate GPS devices instead of my phone since my phone uses up data and the GPS doesn't, saving me $$.

I have only used the Via 1525 a couple of times and it worked perfectly. I had to make a new account to TomTom to update it and overall it took about an hour and a half. I had a couple of problems with the update and had to restart but it finally worked. It comes with a USB for charging from a computer and another to use in the auxiliary power port in the car, and a mounting disk to adhere to a good spot in the car. It's not as intuitive as I would like, but it's not hard to figure out and it took us straight to our destination both times. I purposely passed some streets it was telling to me turn on to just to see how fast it would recalculate a route and it recalculated quickly. It has a lot of options that are indicated on the product page, most of which I will probably not use.

It's too early yet to give it 5 stars, but definitely 4 for now. It's a GPS, it found satellites quickly, got me a route planned out and was easy to follow. What more do I want from it? I like it a lot. It's supposed to have lifetime traffic and lifetime maps.......or until TomTom stops supporting it too.
text_fidelity_b: TomTom Via 1525SE 5 Inch GPS Navigation Device with Free Traffic, Free Maps of the US, Advanced Lane Guidance and Spoken Turn-By-Turn Directions

text_fidelity_a:
Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114) I travel quite a bit and many of the trips I take are short in duration- often only two or three nights. I don’t need a lot of luggage space for these short trips and I like taking backpacks because I can often avoid carry- on and baggage fees if my backpack can fit under my seat. This desire for economical travel led me to get the Case Logic BRYBPR116 Bryker Backpack Roller.

With this Case Logic Backpack, you get a two-in-one backpack and piece of luggage well suited for travel or business. The wheels make it perfect for traversing an airport and with the added straps, you can carry it on your back, like a traditional backpack. There is an outside pocket where you can tuck the straps so they are not hanging out, flopping around when you don’t need them. And the handle can be completely pushed inside the backpack and sealed off with a zipper so that no one sees it. I like these qualities because it means I can make this look like a backpack when I want it to and I can make it look more like a piece of luggage when I want it to.

Inside the backpack, there is a separate compartment for a laptop and I like that you can unsnap this if you like, making for a larger interior space that is just right for stuffing your two- day supply of clothing and personal items. Like I said, my primary usage with this backpack is for travel and I usually don’t take my laptop with me when I’m on a two- day trip, so I would rather have the open space, to make it more like a piece of luggage.

There is one thing to keep in mind if you take this backpack on a plane, and that is the size of pack makes it only barely able to fit under your seat. It will stick out some, so be prepared to have a snug space where your feet normally go. And unlike other backpacks, it’s too rigid- thanks to the handle- to make it collapsible and flexible. To save having to pay carry- on fees on certain airlines, I am willing to place it under the airline seat in front of me regardless, even if it does stick out some. If your flying on an airline that doesn’t charge extra for carry-ons, then this won’t be an issue since you can easily place the backpack in the overhead, which is what I recommend doing. For everyone else, just bear in mind that the length of the backpack makes it a challenge to fit under a seat.

I have a wide assortment of backpacks and luggage in my home to accommodate different needs. This Case Logic rolling backpack is a nice addition to my collection and I like that it performs a dual role. It has suited me well so far and it makes a good choice of luggage/backpack for business people and others who are constantly on the go for short spans of time.
text_fidelity_b: Case Logic Bryker Convertible Backpack (BRYBP114)

text_fidelity_a: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Earbuds Headphones, Earphones with Microphone and Nylon Cable (Turquoise Blue). I have always been a big skullcandy fan (I know, I probably just lost most people reading this review, but hear me out). I am a hipster when it comes to skullcandy, I was skullcandy back in 07-08 when they were actually of quality. No different than the first set of beats that were good, and everything recent is subpar. Now, I continued purchasing skullcandy because I was never good to my earbuds. The average lifespan of my earbuds was about 2 months, so the cheap quality was fine. But when I started med school and had to study all the time, I found my earbuds finally lasted over a year, but the quality was bugging me. They wouldn't cancel out the annoying undergrads who used the library for socialization rather than studying. I decided to finally to invest in pair of higher quality earbuds. I was willing to spend beats price if I was going to get quality. Little did I know there existed a pair of earbuds roughly equal in price to my skullcandy, but outclasses them when it comes to quality. All of my friends who have tried these earbuds have had to switch. They have a great sound, noise cancel, and have a mic if you're into that. The one negative (hence the minus 1 star) is that the jack has this "nub" that when pressed in my pocket pauses my music. This is very annoying for walking to class or the bus. But when I'm sitting and studying, I would choose no other.
text_fidelity_b: Symphonized NRG Premium Genuine Wood In-ear Noise-isolating Earbuds Headphones, Earphones with Microphone and Nylon Cable (Turquoise Blue).

text_fidelity_a: Smart Watches for Women, Sport Fitness Watch with Bluetooth/Heart Rate/Blood Pressure/SpO2/Sleeping Tracker/Pedometer/Multiple Sport Modes, Waterproof Fashion Smart Watch Sync with Google Fit App It was so easy to set this up. It paired with my phone and my Apple watch to get notifications. I included a schedule of the I67 schedule for water resistance. As you can see, you are able to be in water for a small amount of time, and under 5.8mm, otherwise, you will get water damage. So, you really don't want to go swimming with this watch on. Personally, I wouldn't shower with it on or wash dishes with it on. I treat my Apple watch the same way. The connector bases are reinforced at each end of the wire which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug. The connector plug itself is gold plated which is the ultimate standard in connectivity.

This Cat8 Ethernet Cable is 25’ long which makes it absolutely ideal for using it to directly plug your TV or gaming system into your router. So many of us stream programs and movies via our TV and there is no comparison in speed between a WiFi connection and a wired connection. For gamers, it is absolutely the way to go - do away with all lag caused by your WiFi by connecting directly to your router.

You will not find a better 25’ Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that you’ll love.

This is an excellent purchase that you’ll never regret.

However, when I check the time in the night it requires fumbling with the phone, then being half-blinded by the screen when I turn it on long enough to check the time. I looked to this alarm clock to resolve this for me and in terms of timekeeping it’s exactly what I hoped. As a radio, though, it leaves much to be desired.

The main feature of this clock that makes it worth the cost is the tremendous display. The numbers are huge and are red which does not ruin night vision. The projection on the ceiling is also great and I like being able to flip it at the touch of a button. For me, this is all I need.

However, where it fails is in the audio department. The speaker is sub-par and when listening to music to does not do well at all and sounds bad though not awful. I have heard worse. I would rather see this sell for $10 more and have a better speaker in it.

If you choose this alarm clock, get it for the display which is great and is the main selling point. If you are looking for a good clock radio and the sound is important to you, this might not be the best choice. I don’t care about the audio so this is a minor point; others may feel differently.

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin nüvi 265/265T 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Traffic I previously owned a Garmin Nuvi 360 which I loved. I specifically need a GPS that includes Bluetooth, since I use it both for directions and for hands-free phone use (which is rare, but important when I need it). I loved my 360 and used it daily until just a few months ago, when the Bluetooth suddenly stopped working. After troubleshooting with Garmin's tech support, it was determined the unit would need to be sent in for service, and since it was out of warranty, the flat charge for service was $79, which didn't include insured shipping costs.

Well, do the math. Obviously, one can acquire a brand-new GPS for not much more than $79, so I started shopping. That's how I ended up with my new Garmin Nuvi 265T. And I LOVE IT! I'm almost glad that my old unit went on the fritz, because it gave me an excuse to upgrade to this newer, fantastic unit.

The 360 was great for accurate directions, easy to see and read display, and consistent Bluetooth (until it broke). Here's how the 265T is even better:

- Smaller, lighter, and thinner, but with a slightly wider screen.
- No "antenna" on the back to flip up and fiddle with - it just works.
- Uses my existing mount (from ProClips), so no change to that was necessary.
- Includes FREE traffic notifications, which so far seem to work pretty well.
- When you power it on, it seems to bypass the warning screen that you need to "Agree" to quicker, and then shows a simple display: Where To, and View Map. On the 360, if you didn't do anything else, it would sit on the menu indefinitely, but the 265T automatically switches to map display after a few minutes if you don't select anything else. Basically, you can start your car and just forget about it, until you need it!

The traffic feature is ad-supported, so occasionally very small banner-type ads appear on the display, usually offering coupons for local restaurants etc. They are quite small and not intrusive in any way, so I don't mind them. I guess there's also an option to upgrade to a paid traffic service that would not include ads, but I don't see a need for that for my own use.

In general I am thrilled with Garmin products, and this Nuvi 265T is no exception. What a great deal, and a nice early Christmas present for myself!
text_fidelity_b: Garmin nüvi 265/265T 3.5-Inch Bluetooth Portable GPS Navigator with Traffic

text_fidelity_a:
JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black I wasn't expecting much given the price of this item, and I got pretty much what I expected.

The charging port is hard to reach and the LED charging indicator is difficult, if not impossible to see, without having to move the foam earpiece covering.

Setting up/pairing the device is pretty easy. Press the button for 4 seconds or so and you’ll hear a pleasant female voice say, “Hello”. This means the power is on. Continue holding the button and the device will enter pairing mode. You’ll hear the voice say, “Ready to pair.” When pairing is complete, you’ll hear the device say, “You’re connected” and tell you how much charge the battery has. So far, all I’ve heard is, “Battery full.” I have no idea what other battery indications the voice will give – perhaps only at 3/4, 1/2 and 1/4? Or maybe percentages?

The buttons are the biggest drawback with this device. Actually, it's really just one multi-function button on the right earpiece. The button functionality is not like any Bluetooth headset I've used before - very non-intuitive. The button has no label at all and the tactile feedback is nonexistent at times - I press the button sometimes and there's no "click" feeling. If a song is playing, it doesn't seem to matter where I press, the song stops if it is playing. When I press again, anywhere, it starts playing again.

There is no volume control on the headphones at all. You’ll have to adjust the volume from your phone/audio player. There is a bare bones EQ function. You control this by clicking the multi-function button 3 times in rapid succession. Each time you do this, the device advances to the next of 3 EQ setting – balanced, bass boost and JLab signature. The “balanced” setting seems to sound just like what it’s named – balanced or equal high, mid and low tones. The bass boos is decent – not overbearing. Not sure what the last one is, but if the pictograms in the manual are any indication, it boost the high and low ends. The EQ function does provide audible feedback – the voice announces each setting by name.

There's a next track function, but no function for going to the previous track. The next track function requires holding down the multi-function button for 2 seconds. There's no audible feedback for this function (other than a very short moment of silence). When you hear the silence, let go IMMEDIATELY. If you hold the button down for too long the Bluetooth connection will be severed and you'll have to reconnect.

Apparently, there's no ability to fast forward or rewind within a song or audio book. You'll have to do this on your phone/audio player. Pretty poor design if you ask me. BTW – I use this only with my audio player, so I did not test the phone/mic functions, but I’d be surprised if they were robust.

The instructions are minimal at best. The manual is one piece of paper printed on 2 sides. Unfolded, it's about the size of 2 business cards - about 4"x4.5" (10.16cm x 11.43cm). One side has instructions and the other is all promotions/disclaimers, etc. That's it.

Sound quality is acceptable - decent bass and stereo separation is good. I’m no audiophile though. The product description says it has "Noise Isolation", which is marketing speak used by all on-ear headphone manufacturers. It simply means the ambient noise is slightly reduced because the headphones cover your ears. Bottom line - there's no tech/function in this device that does any active noise cancellation.

The headphones are a little snug/tight, but not so much to be uncomfortable - at least that's my opinion after an hour+ of testing. Not sure if this will be true for something like a 3-4 hour flight. I’ll test this out in the near future and will update this review, if possible.

The charging cable that comes with the item is 9” long (22.86cm). Not very useful at all, but better than nothing.

On the plus side, the manufacturer did provide an extra set of foam earpiece covers - the set that comes on the headphones is orange. The extra set is black.

Bottom line, for $15 I wasn't expecting a lot - well maybe better button functionality, but hey, what can you do? As my granddad used to say, “You pays your money and you takes your chances.”
text_fidelity_b: JLab Rewind Wireless Retro Headphones | Bluetooth 4.2 | 12 Hours Playtime | Custom EQ3 Sound | Music Controls | Noise Isolation | with Microphone | Throwback 80s 90s Design | Black

I have nsvt but my heart rate generally runs low. So I'm very sensitive when I have palpitations - when this watch kept saying my heart rate was over 95 I wasnt buying it. That brings into question any other readings or parameters.

I find the watch annoying and frustrating to use. The watch face does not interact very well for me. I'm constantly trying to tap it and it wont register so then the screen shuts off. Another annoying thing is it tells you to start moving around when I'm doing housework. I guess you can shut that off but I've really lost interest. Hopefully Garmin can offer some fix for the reading since its past the return date.

The positives - watch is comfortable and I don't wear jewelry. I forget its on. Its a large size so its readable if you have vision issues. I've had no problem with that.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin Venu Sq Music, GPS Smartwatch with Bright Touchscreen Display, Features Music and Up to 6 Days of Battery Life, Slate and Moss Green

While my TV would allow me to connect to the sound bar via Bluetooth I opted to connect via the HDMI ARC connection to avoid any sound lag. In addition to these 2 connection options you can connect via the included optical cable.

I followed the instructions - plugged the HDMI cable (not included) into the ARC HDMI port, plugged the sound bar and subwoofer into the surge protector and turned everything on. The TV automatically recognized the soundbar and changed my output.

All I had to do was press the “secure link” button on the remote and the sound bar wirelessly linked to the subwoofer without issue.

I decided to move the subwoofer to another area of the room - I unplugged it, moved it, plugged it back in and it reconnected without any problem.

I was able to pair the system with my iPhone without any issue and the sound is stunning. From the rich bass of the subwoofer, the vibrant midtones, to the crisp highs - every note is clear and distinct.

While I have a true 5.1 surround system most of the TV broadcasts are not going to utilize that type of system and the sound is actually richer through a sound bar with a subwoofer.

This soundbar can be easily wall mounted using the included template.

The entire system is intuitive and user friendly. While many sound systems require hours to hook up and figure out how to use correctly this one is so straightforward. The remote doesn’t have a bunch of excess buttons that you’ll never need or use.

In my instance my TV remote was able to control it immediately with no issues.

I highly recommend this soundbar for anyone looking for an easy way to improve the quality of the sound from your TV - and you’ll be pleasantly surprised by the rich sound it will deliver regardless of what you play through it.

ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs What I like about this monitor:
1. Easy to set up - I used my previous monitor video cable and power cord and had it up and running in a few minutes.
2. Very clear resolution despite having an old video card.
3. It has an HDMI connection but I am using the regular VGA input and it still very clear.
4. A VGA and sound cord are included.
5. Very sleek, streamline black design which goes nicely with my other computer accessories.

What could be better:
1. The included instructions tell you nothing about how to make video and audio adjustments. I can't use a bright setting and it took a good while to figure out how to use the buttons underneath the screen. They are not intuitive at all.
2. Poor Audio - if you want good audio from this monitor that will not be possible. It is a thin monitor and the audio is very thin and tinny. I was hoping I could disconnect my external sound system to make more room on my desk but found out that I must keep it if I want to hear any decent sound from my computer.
3. While testing the volume on this monitor you must still figure out how to toggle using the various buttons underneath. There is no single volume button or toggle switch. And it will not get very loud.
4. If you don't bump the monitor or use the toggle switches the monitor stays fairly steady on it's stand. Otherwise it will rock and jiggle while using the buttons.
5. No HDMI cable is included.

The scant instructions did say to visit their website to download the latest drivers but as of yet this monitor is not listed in their driver drop down window. I don't think that matter much at this time as the monitor is very clear and sharp.
Overall: Good monitor for the price (as of this review it costs $138.24 Prime) which I feel is a fair price.
text_fidelity_b: ViewSonic VA2359-SMH 23 Inch IPS 1080p LED Monitor with HDMI and VGA Inputs

text_fidelity_a:
HDMI to Mini DisplayPort,QGeeM 4K x 2K HDMI Male to Mini DP Female Adapter Converter for HDMI Equipped Systems,Compatible with VESA Dual Mode DisplayPort 1.2,HDMI 1.4 I guess it’s good that somebody makes this adapter, but it doesn’t work as described and its housing is so much fatter than a standard HDMI, it renders neighboring ports useless. I thoroughly checked the product info before ordering and it didn’t work. I called tech support, who insisted it would work, and sent me another. Now I see in the comments, this item often does not work with Apple LED Cinema Displays. I believe one reviewer may be correct, that this is not mini display port, but thunderbolt (and while there are times the two work together, such as plugging a MDP monitor into a TB port on a Mac, adapters are a situation in which it matters which is which).

Even if it did work, it’s so much fatter than a typical HDMI cable, it blocks the ports next to it. In this case, it blocks my thunderbolt connection, turning my solution for using 2 MDP displays back into, only being able to use one.

I’m not sure if it’s relevant that the input on the adapter is strangely shallow, so the MDP doesn’t even slide in all the way.

In short I imagine this is fine for a narrow margin of the people seeking this adapter. But it does not work on all the devices it claims to, it might not be MDP after all, and it causes as many problems as it solves in a crowded input situation.
text_fidelity_b: HDMI to Mini DisplayPort,QGeeM 4K x 2K HDMI Male to Mini DP Female Adapter Converter for HDMI Equipped Systems,Compatible with VESA Dual Mode DisplayPort 1.2,HDMI 1.4

I don't do Podcasts or self-centric Youtube videos. But, I DO videos about drones and quadcopters. Some of which, I narrate. I've always wanted to have a better audio experience for my viewers. The cage is the perfect example of how to isolate 'telegraphed' noise from your desk or table, preventing unwanted noise in your recording. (roll eyes) The connections are standard, the three prong mic connection can be swapped out for any length you happen to have around. The other end is a standard 3.5mm 4 c jack (designed for splitting the signal between your recording device and headphones). But, it can be used without the splitter pigtail, in case you don't need the feedback. You can tell from my brief video, the recorded sound is very good. Great purchase, five stars.

text_fidelity_a:
Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer) UPDATE: Local retailer slashed prices and a buddy bought a new +2 (new packaging) and found : new packaging doesn't come with HDMI cable, or the external mic adaptor. He promptly returned it and got an "old packaging" and now had all the equipment. Why the "new packaging" costs more than the "old packaging" is beyond me. The "new packaging" mimics the Roam2 packaging, with no see thru "bubble" at the top of the box - BEWARE!!!

FYI - BB discontinuing the Contour line and the mounts are all 50% off, and the camera(s) are $100 off.

This is a dual review, as I own both the Contour + 2 and the Contour Roam2. I don't work for nor do I have any affiliation with Contour. I've had the Roam2 for more than 6 months, but held off writing this review until I had the +2 to compare it to. Although I don't own a GoPro, several friends do and I do their video editing so I'll chime in on the Contour vs. GoPro at the end.

MOUNTS:
Contour uses the same proprietary mounts across their lineup, so interchangeability between the two should be fairly easy (but doesn't always work out that way). I've found some to be flimsy(hat mount), while others are damn near bomb proof(suction cup)! The rotating lens means you can mount it in just about any position, however it is difficult to know that you've framed the shot with the correct orientation! Had an important video recorded upside down - laser level only lets you know it's level, not if it's upside down! One of the best features I've found is the ¼ by 20 thread on the bottom of the Contour, pretty much universal to all modern cameras and there's a TON of mounts out there reasonably priced.

SOFTWARE:
The Storyteller program needs to be installed on your computer and is fairly easy to use, but not intuitive, you need to play around a bit before you can figure everything out. The editing ability is extremely limited. (I use imovie). Software is free, and although you can use the camera(s) without first updating I suggest you do that first! The +2 also has an app that I use on my iPhone 5 - it too is free and pretty easy to use - but not as capable as the Storyteller program. The downside is you HAVE to use the Storyteller program to change settings on the Roam2, AND you have to use it if you want to use any of the GPS data with the +2.

ROAM2:
Got this for Xmas last year and immediately swapped the included 4GB micro SD for a 16GB. SUPER easy to use - charge, point, and slide the slider to the on position. Video quality is good, first few outings I had it set for 1080@30 and was very happy. In editing I found one clip I had to slow down and was slightly disappointed at the quality - since then I've got it set for 720@60 and haven't had any issues - video quality is still good (even in slow mo). Low light does induce more "noise" to the video, but if there's ambient light (streetlights etc.) you can still get decent vids. Sound quality isn't all that, it's usable, but in high winds or at speed - forget it. Battery life is really good at around 2 hours. The camera itself is very well built, one of my first uses it got throw (by an idiot) about 8ft into about 4 inches of water over concrete - few scratches, but still kept recording. This led me to look for something to help protect the aluminum body - Glock Tape, works amazing, adds some protection, but most importantly gives it some GRIP!

[[ASIN:B00C7WXTJS 6-Pack Glock Grip Tape - Pistol Grip Tape. * Use on handguns and rifles * Not gritty like sandpaper or skateboard tape. * Does not scuff clothing, holsters, furniture or car seats like those sandy tapes. * Makes chambering a round easier for arthritis s...]]

CONTOUR +2:
Only had it for a week or so, really wanted it due to the Bluetooth (to help frame shots) and was wanted the waterproof housing (worried about watersports damage on an upcoming trip) the GPS would be a plus. Once again amazing build quality - this things tough as nails. First thing I did was hook up to Storyteller and get the latest firmware update - less than 5 minutes later I was off and running! Pairing the Bluetooth took a couple of attempts, but once connected has excellent range (20 or so feet with obstructions - close to 50ft line of sight!). Using the app you can check status of battery, GPS, and memory as well as change settings and start stop recording - wish you could watch videos but oh well. The app has about a one second delay between what the camera "sees" and what you see on your phone - pretty amazing! Attached to my suction cup mount and went for a drive - took about 30 seconds for the GPS to lock on the first time (since then it only takes maybe 5 seconds). GPS is accurate. The video quality is great! Uploaded vid into storyteller and the GPS data was also great - until I exported it then there was a lag of about 5 seconds between the data being displayed and the video. Waterproof housing is bulky, yet seems a bit flimsy - still not sure it could survive 200 ft of water. Came with HDMI to hook up to TV - works really well. Haven't used the mic adaptor yet. Battery life seems to be around 1.5 hours, but spare batteries are cheap.

[[ASIN:B007PUC1UU Wasabi Power Battery and Charger Kit for Contour 2350, 2450, 2900, C010410K and ContourHD, ContourGPS, Contour+, Contour+2]]

COMPARISON:
Even though the video specs are the same between the +2 and the Roam2, the video quality of the +2 is noticeably better - even in low light. Sound quality on both suffers in high winds or speed. They both have the proprietary T-rail mounts on both sides, but the ¼ by 20 thread is about an inch further back on the +2. The Roam2 is waterproof without housing to about 3ft, but the +2 has the waterproof housing. The +2 also allows for filming while charging. The +2 has the HDMI out, as well as a jack for external mic. The +2 has the Bluetooth app, plus GPS - that combined with replaceable batteries and the better video make it worth the extra money.

CONTOUR vs. GOPRO:
I absolutely love the form factor and the mounting options available for the Contours. The Contour line has their own proprietary mounts, but the ability to use the ¼ by 20 thread mounts for other cameras (even the GoPro mounts) plus the rotating lens means there's just more ways to mount the Contour. That being said the GoPro Hero3 flat out destroys the video quality of the Roam2, and slightly edges out the +2. Of course this difference (even over the Roam2) is completely removed once video is uploaded to Youtube or other sharing sites as they compress the video during upload! I've yet to see a GoProH3 recording 1080 go for more than 75 minutes. Sound quality between all three is about the same. The GoProH3 app uses wifi - and has about a 3-4 second delay - still works for framing shots, but not much else. The GoPro also has the advantage in that you can change settings in camera - but it is a complicated affair(the +2 only allows you to choose between two predetermined settings). GoProH3 doesn't have GPS, or rotating lense. Contour recently lowered the price on the +2 it's now $50 cheaper than the GoProH3. Also it seems they changed pricing on their mounts - I went with the Contour line because of the simplicity of their system, more mounts, cheaper price, and the form factor. Now that they're cheaper it's a no brainer.
text_fidelity_b: Contour +2 - Old Packaging (Discontinued by Manufacturer)

text_fidelity_a:
Pentax K1000 Manual Focus SLR Film Camera with Pentax 50mm Lens My k1000 will be 30 years old this Christmas, and it has been the most reliable camera I have ever owned. My lenses are still nice and sharp. My light meter and flash shoe still work. I have probably changed the battery 3 times. There are no light leaks. Everything works just like the day I got it.

This is a great first camera for any person who wants to learn about photography: exposure, composition, etc. With digital point and shoots, it's really easy to just be a documentarian and rely on photoshop or filters to fix things up a bit later, but there's no real incentive to get things right in the first instance. Film - real film - requires patience and discipline and a critical eye. Which is why I am teaching my 11 year old son to use this.

A tip on loading the film (I was dead broke for a lot of the first decade I owned this and could not afford to waste a bit): Before you try to load the film, bend just the last little bit down, so that it makes a little l-shaped piece that will catch in the slot. Put the tag into the slot and carefully pull out just enough to fit the film snugly into the camera. BY HAND, turn the spool on the left side about half a turn to set the film on the spool and make sure the holes are caught on the teeth. When you turn the left spool, the film should come easily out of the canister. Only do a little bit, and if it seems to be working (i.e. pulling the film out of the canister), close the back of the camera. Cock the camera - WATCH the film counter to make sure the film is advancing. If it's not, don't rewind unless you are sure you can do so without losing your leading edge into the film canister. Just open the back and re-set the edge onto the spool and try again. If it is - and you should be able to feel the resistance in the mechanism - shoot a picture. The first one won't come out. The second one may, and by loading carefully, you should be able to get an extra couple of shots on every roll of film.
text_fidelity_b: Pentax K1000 Manual Focus SLR Film Camera with Pentax 50mm Lens

Headphone Adapter Converter Supports Audio and Charging for Motorola MotoZ, Letv ,2 in 1 USB-C to 3.5mm Audio Adapter, Nylon Braided 2 in 1 USB Type C Cable Fast Charge to 3.5mm Audio Jack(Black) This is a much easier alternative to the My K-cup option if you want to use your own coffee in a K-cup machine rather than the pre-packaged cups. Unlike the My K-cup you don't need to remove the inner cup of the machine to use this. It just drops right in, so you can switch between this and a regular k-cup without having to dismantle anything.

The kit is very complete. There are three cups, each a slightly different color (different shades of brown). The cups are decently made. The plastic sides are nice and thick; the o-ring on the cap is of good quality; and the metal mesh is firmly attached. My only quibble with the build quality is the hinge. It's plastic, and I don't have confidence that it will last a long time before breaking. It's not a big deal, since the cup will still work fine even with a broken hinge, so I'm not docking any points due to that potential problem.

I like that the water dispersion channel has slots all around it to ensure water gets sprayed in all directions inside the cup to keep the grounds uniformly wet. I also really like that the lip area has a slight indent to make it very easy to pop open the top with one hand.

It fit fine in my Cuisinart K-cup machine. The lid of the machine was just slightly raised compared with using a "real" k-cup, but it had zero impact on performance. I tried several different brews, all with good results. You will need to fiddle with the grind level to get the best coffee. Too fine of a grind and it gets over-extracted and bitter; too coarse and it's weak.

Cleaning a used cup is very easy. I pop open the top, hold it upside down in the compost pail, and whack it gently on the base with a wooden spoon. Nearly all the used grounds drop out, and what's left can be easily rinsed under running water. You can also just dump the contents into the disposal or garbage if you don't compost your grounds.

Another option is to use a mini filter in the cup. A package of them are included and, while they do make cleanup easier, I prefer to use just the cup without a filter.

The kit also includes a charcoal filter. I didn't use that, so I can't speak to its performance. It looks to be the same size as the filters used in the water intake of my Cuisinart K-cup machine, so I expect it would perform in a similar fashion.

This Smart Cup kit works well, is well-made/designed, and comes in a very complete kit. Having used the My K-cup version I can confidently say that this performs better and is easier to use. Highly recommend.

text_fidelity_a:
Olympus OM-D E-M1 16MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3-Inch LCD (Body Only) (Silver w/ Black Trim) I have been shooting Olympus cameras since 1978. I have always loved the lenses. With over 2,000,000 shots on my Olympus E-500 camera, I decided it was time to invest in a new camera.

I was reluctant at first to try the EM-1 for three reasons:
- The format is Micro-Four Thirds, not Four Thirds. I take 99% of my photos in the telephoto range, and that is what Four Thirds was optimized to use. Micro-Four Thirds is geared more towards wide angle lenses.
- The camera is mirrorless and uses an electronic Viewfinder (EVF).
- I have to use a converter to mount my existing Four Thirds lenses, and converters have a very bad history.

Out of the box:
The first thing that you notice when you pull the body out is that it is SOLID. The thing feels like it is built like a tank. I have not tried the "splashproof" and other claims, but just holding this body I can believe them. The camera fits well in my hand. My hands are a little large, and my pinky occasionally slides off the bottom. I may buy the grip/extra battery holder later if this proves to be a problem. YMMV.

Using Four Thirds lenses:
I have no Micro Four Thirds lenses and a lot invested in Four Thirds lenses, so using them was a key issue. Olympus has 1/17 or 1 MP of the sensor dedicated to phase detection auto focus, the only type of auto focus that will work with these lenses. I find that the system works very well. Focusing is fast and accurate.

Mounting the converter is easy, as expected. Once mounted, you use a button on the side to release the lens. This is a learning issue since I still normally hit the lens release button on the camera body. I anticipate little real problems with this since as soon as I try to put the cover on the back of the lens I realize my error.

Balance with the 12-60 mm Four Thirds lens is excellent. Holding the lens by the zoom collar, the weight is only slightly behind my left hand. I only have to support the body lightly with my right hand. I personally like that balance. Longer lenses like the 70-300 are also well balanced.

EVF:
I have used a mirrored SLR since 1978 and a rangefinder 35 mm camera and 126 film P&S cameras before that. As you might guess, I favor a direct view to see what I am shooting. EVF have issues with resolution and lag when moving to a different point of interest or following a subject, especially in low light.

The EVF has turned out to be great. I really like Olympus' implementation. There is some lag, but it is generally minimal. The "What You See Is What You Get" is a big plus in my book. Adjust the exposure compensation or manual exposure settings, and the view in the EVF changes to reflect what the image will look like. It is not perfect, but it gets 95%+ of what you will actually get. The display of settings is bright, clear, crisp, large, and surprisingly unobtrusive.

The EVF also allows a lot of changes in camera settings to be done without removing the camera from your eye. Use the two dials, and you can see where the focus points that you are using are. Hit the OK button on the back, and you can use the dials to adjust just about every setting while watching the selections you are making in the EVF. Ditto with the other buttons like HDR and auto exposure mode.

HDR:
I had the opportunity to use in-camera HDR while on a recent trip. The day was cloudy, and there was a lot of shadow against bright grey clouds. The in-camera HDR used a series of shots at different exposures and combined them in the camera. The results were better than HDR Pro in Photoshop CS5.5 IMO. I was much, much happier with the dynamic range and overall look of the images. the 10 fps shooting mode was also great for minimizing camera movement, ghosts and other problems associated with HDR.

Image stabilization:
The EM-1 has a five axis image stabilization system for the sensor. That means any lens becomes can be used. The fourth and fifth axes are for rotations. One compensates for the slight turn of the camera that often occurs when you press the shutter button. I had good success using IS in low light with my 70-300 mm lens set at 300 mm.

Scenes:
the EM-1 has many useful scene modes. I used landscape and panorama with great success. The artistic filters and story modes may also interest you. I prefer to do those types of things in post-processing.

ISO:
The camera has an almost insane 25600 maximum ISO. Yes, you get image quality degradation and noise at that ISO, but the in-camera JPEG processor can actually give you some relief from the problems at higher ISOs. I so far have found shooting up to ISO 1600 produces no discerned degradation. I tried ISO 6400 and found minimal issues.

For those who started with film and were in love with the "high ISO" 1000 film for low light shooting, this is a major and welcome advancement. For those newer to photography that have been using higher ISO cameras for a while, the speed may not be much of a gain, but the image quality should be.

The low end ISO is 200, which is the new normal. I do not find it to be a problem. I would rather shoot at a faster shutter speed than have an ISO 100 setting in most cases. There is an ISO LOW setting, but I do not plan to use it. If you regularly shoot in bright light and want lower f-stops, invest in a neutral density filter.

Back display:
The back display is slightly disappointing. It can only tilt up and down, not rotate so that you can see your composition when you are getting into the shot. It works well for shooting over crowds or getting a low angle shot.

On the plus side, the display is clear, bright and a touchscreen that can be used to select a point of interest for focusing and can be used to take the shot in live view mode. You can also use it to select settings to change. The next generation should be even better, and hopefully it will have a screen that rotates.

SD card:
One change from the E-500 that I do not like is the use of SD rather than CF cards. CF cards are nearly indestructible, and a good Sansdisk Extreme card works virtually anywhere, anytime and is virtually impossible to physically break. The xD card slot disappearing is no loss, but not having a second card slot is somewhat surprising given the high-end prosumer/professional positioning of this camera.

Controls and customization:
The controls are pretty well placed for me with the exception of the auto exposure lock button. That is right beside the viewfinder and too far to the left for my liking. You can do a lot of customization with the control buttons and dials, but there are limits. I have not made any changes yet because I am still learning the camera. Overall the defaults seem logical and useful.

This camera has two dials, one on the front and one on the back. The E-500 only had a back dial, so I am learning to use the two dial system. They work well for adjusting and selecting options. I think the second dial was a good addition. Both are conveniently located for my fingers.

Image quality:
All of this is meaningless if the image you get out is bad. The EM-1 does not disappoint. I know that there are people who insist that they need 48 MP or some other ridiculously large number. The reality is that 16 MP is a great size for printing full-size 300 dpi images on your printer or using a commercial photo printing service. If all you do is screen displays, it is about eight times more pixels than you need for a typical 2 MP monitor.

The quality of the EM-1 pixels is very high, and you get excellent out-of-the-camera RAW and JPEG images. I have no problems seeing fine detail at 100% and higher magnifications.

Summary:
This camera is a winner, and it works with my existing Four Thirds lenses so I do not have to invest another $3000+ in lenses to use it. I have a lot to learn, and it will take some time to get the most out of the camera, but out-of-the-box, using my E-500 techniques, it is already doing great work.
text_fidelity_b: Olympus OM-D E-M1 16MP Mirrorless Digital Camera with 3-Inch LCD (Body Only) (Silver w/ Black Trim)

ZUGU CASE for iPad Air Gen 4 & 5 10.9 Inch (2020/2022) - Protective, Ultra Thin, Magnetic Stand, Sleep/Wake Cover - Berry Purple I spent days shopping for the ideal case for my new Apple Air 4th generation tablet. I shopped at a variety of stores. I was surprised to find that some of the companies known for sturdy cell phone cases did not offer the same quality to fit tablets. Notably absent was protection for the corners.
My search finally paid off as the ZUGU case is ideal. it is sturdy without excessive bulk. It protects all sides of the tablet including the corners. The cover projects a bit above both the camera lens and the tablet screen to protect them. The stand folds easily on the outside of the case. It is thin but stiff enough to hold the tablet at various angles and the magnetic attachment is a unique feature, securing the device without slippage. (I observed that some cases can flop unpredictably or are very limited in their options for viewing angles.)
Given the snug fit, I found it initially a challenge to attach the ZUGU case. . This is before I found the best approach was to slip the top right hand corner of the case last over the tablet frame. Due to the openings, the case material was s thinner and more flexible here. But do be careful not to pull too hard: The corner should slip readily over the frame here if the remaining sides are snug.
Another unique feature is that the company may offer to cover the copay if the owner has Apple Care and the screen breaks. (Please check the manufacturer website for detail).I
There is one trade.off with the case: it is purely functional rather than being a fashion statement. But I personally prefer protection to good looks and will enclose it with some confidence in a tote.

text_fidelity_a:
SanDisk 32GB Class 4 SDHC Memory Card, Frustration-Free Packaging- SDSDB-032G-AFFP (Label May Change) This review is of the 64GB SDHX card. I use it for a specific purpose: backing up my document folders on my two laptops. It works perfectly with my Windows XP systems over ancient USB 2.0 ports. I can still back up a full card in less than an hour, and if I were on a more modern system with USB 3.0 it would take only a fraction of that time.

This particular card will NOT work in my Samsung Galaxy Note II (I had to try anyway). In fact, make sure your device will actually accept SDHX cards before purchaing this 64GB model or you may be disappointed. Most Microsoft Windows systems running XP service pack 2 or later, Windows CE and Server 2003 will recognize this card, as will Mac OS X Snow Leopard 10.6.5 or later. Phones, tablets and devices running Microsoft Windows RT will also recognize this card. Beyond that check first.

Back to how I use this card: the price for this card is around forty bucks at the time of this review. I could have gotten an exernal hard drive in the terabyte range for twice that, but this has no moving parts, fits in my wallet and with a [[ASIN:B00FSDKBYY Sabrent SuperSpeed USB 3.0 Flash Memory Card Reader]] plugs into any computer (with an operating system that supports the format) via USB ports. For me it's convenient, especially since I am only backing up working documents and never come close to the 64GB capacity (which is closer to 56GB formatted.) In fact I use two of these in rotation for safety, overwriting the older one completely since it takes less than an hour. I always keep the other one on my person.

As the SDHX standard becomes more established and ubiquitous this type of card may work with more devices. At 64GB this is probably the smallest size since the SDHX format was designed to accomodate up to two terabytes. So unless you have a device that is compatible with this format, or you are using it for a single purpose on a supported operating system, you may want to get an SDHC card instead.
text_fidelity_b: SanDisk 32GB Class 4 SDHC Memory Card, Frustration-Free Packaging- SDSDB-032G-AFFP (Label May Change)

text_fidelity_a:
ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included) When I initially saw this camera it checked most of the boxes I look for when looking for security cameras. It is PoE, has H.265, ONVIF support allowing use with Blue Iris, Sony IMX274 Starvis Sensor. Once I received this camera and began digging into it I quickly realized certain important facts.

Most importantly, this is a rebranded Hikvision camera. This is among the companies that has been discovered spying on the US using their cameras - the firmware this camera comes with is long outdated and, in fact, can not be updated to anywhere close to what is current. This is far too risky for me to install on my system.

Any camera you install on your system should have the latest firmware installed and you need to have a good understanding of network security protocols. Cameras such as this one, that are older versions of cameras made by manufacturers that are blacklisted - while still being sold, people who understand the industry avoid them - are an invitation for hackers to invade your system.

While the specs on and price of this camera seem decent - this is not a camera I recommend. This poses far more risks than it is worth.
text_fidelity_b: ANNKE C800 4K 8MP PoE Security Camera with Audio Recording, 4K Ultra HD IP Turret Camera, 100ft EXIR 2.0 Night Vision, H.265+, IP67 Weatherproof, Support 256GB SD Card(Not Included)

Edimax Bluetooth Adapter for PC, BT 5.0 EDR Nano USB Dongle, Fast Transfer, for BT Headphones Headset Speakers Keyboard Mouse, Win 10/11 Plug-n-Play, Linux: 2.6.32-6.2, Mint 21 Plug-n-Play, BT-8500 I use this to stream audio to my TWS headphones so I can listen to music, videos, and audio books while working out or doing projects around the house. I've been using it for about a month now, and I'm pretty satisfied with it.

It worked on plug-in with Manjaro KDE, and integrated with the OS without any additional configuration. It reliably auto-connects and the system even routes audio to it while it is connected, and then restores it to my main headphones when it is not.

Audio quality is decent, about what you would expect from something like this. Not as good as a direct connection obviously, but for most non-critical listening this is perfectly sufficient. Just make sure your headphones support the higher bitrate codecs - I knew mine didn't, but double check to be sure. I have some Bose Soundsport Free headphones which are vented, which is great because I can hear what's going on around the house, but they don't support any advanced codec at all. So I end up with about a 500ms delay on the audio. That's fine for me - if I'm at my desk, I'm using my main headphones anyway, but just be aware.

Range is tricky. With the Soundsports, it's pretty bad, maybe twenty feet in open air, ten feet if there's any obstruction. I have some Sony WF-1000XM4 TWS earbuds and they do better, but only by about 50%. If you are going more than 15ft from the source, you may have issues. However, my system is close to a wireless router and a UPS, so that may be interfering in my case.

Broadly, for this price, I'd recommend this. Sure you can look for higher quality transmitters that go for $50-$100, but until you pull the trigger on that, this should serve your purposes fine.
text_fidelity_b: Edimax Bluetooth Adapter for PC, BT 5.0 EDR Nano USB Dongle, Fast Transfer, for BT Headphones Headset Speakers Keyboard Mouse, Win 10/11 Plug-n-Play, Linux: 2.6.32-6.2, Mint 21 Plug-n-Play, BT-8500

5GHz Light Bulb Security Camera Wi-Fi Outdoor, 360° Lightbulb Security Camera 1080P Wireless, Color Night Vision, Motion Detection, Compatible with Alexa/Google I upgraded from my 1st generation Petcube to this one, because I was looking for something that didn’t require a subscription to view a full days worth of footage. Also, being gen 1, my old camera’s video quality is very low and there is no night vision.
No subscription needed (if you install a micro and card). They do offer a cloud storage option, which is nice, and they offer an option to insert a micro and card to store locally- which is exactly what I was looking for. I just popped out my card out of my Nintendo switch to test it out.
This arrived packaged neat in the box shown. I was able to put this together in a rush, as I was in the middle of moving and I wanted to be able to watch my pups while I was go for an hour or so. I downloaded the app and connected the camera- all in less than 2-3 minutes. There were no hiccups. Just set up and go.
This little security camera began picking up motion and sound right away (fyi, you need to go into settings to switch on the alerts). On day 2 of having this installed, I caught one of my pups jumping over his pen. Thankfully, the app alerted me, and I was able to rush back and get him back in before he did any damage to himself. text_fidelity_a:
KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black) Best sounding in-ear headphones I've ever heard, by a mile. I've owned the Bang and Olufsen H3, Sony XBA H1, Klipsch S4, X7, X6i, 1More Dual Drivers, Beats by Dr Dre Tour (wired), and Monster Cable's Jamz and Turbines.

The bass has lots of range and goes DEEP, in some tracks it even reminds me of my Kicker CVR 12' car subwoofer I used to blast about 15 years ago. It is not quite that overpowering, of course, and it balances out nicely with the other frequencies. The midrange is very present and natural sounding judging by how vocals and guitar strings sound. The highs are beautiful, they sound very accurate to me and present no sibilance. The overall sound is very rich and detailed, it allows you to follow specific instruments as you listen, and it even presents some soundstage (which I didn't think was possible in in-ears, maybe my aforementioned B&O H3 had some)

Overall these do have a V sound signature with boosted bass and treble, but not as marked as almost everything else that's in the market. In order to eliminate any fatigue caused by this, I would strongly recommend that you disable any bass boost, make sure you're not elevating bass or treble at all in EQ, and go even deeper and disable default features like Dolby Atmos (Oneplus phone) and even the Hi Fi quad DAC on LG phones (which I've found does introduce a bit of a V curve itself)

Other than their sound these earphones' build quality seems very good and durable. I'm in disbelief they could cost $60. You're welcome
text_fidelity_b: KZ ZS10 Pro, Linsoul 4BA+1DD 5 Driver in Ear Monitor, HiFi Metal Earphones, with Stainless Steel Faceplate, 2 Pin Detachable Cable (Without Mic, Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black) An astonishing example of technology like nothing I've ever seen before.

It's been forty years (!) since I first saw a video camera in high school, a big b/w camera with a backpack that contained the batteries and internals. It was impressive! Then we used a kind of mini-VHS video recorder to share kid videos with our parents maybe 15-20 years ago. Then I got an iPhone which had kind-of video capabilities. So I guess I was ripe to be blown away by this Sony FRAX53/B.

It's small and compact, like a small football. The swing-out screen is breathtakingly crisp and the internal operating system and menus are not only in color, but accompanied by clear, bright sound! I charged the battery and took a video of one of my cats. I could not believe the clarity of the image when I viewed it on the screen! The video is of such high quality that it's easy to overlook the still camera, which is remarkable. High-resolution, bright images. The "Photo" button is kind of oddly placed, it's not easy to operate it while you're holding the device with its right-side hand strap. You can also use a "Manual" mode and twist the lens to achieve custom focus. There's a 20X optical magnification which ought to satisfy anyone.

The Sony software is thorough and functional. The camcorder will transfer photos and video wirelessly if you have a fairly modern computer. I had to use a PC laptop rather than my elderly Mac. That meant using Windows 10, which led to some baffling moments trying to figure out if anything was working.

Between the Sony software and the camcorder and our WiFi setup and Windows 10 I found that the best thing to do sometimes was just WAIT. Windows would give me bad information and I would misinterpret that as an error. Ignore what Windows is telling you and be patient while the FDRAX53/B does its work.

The printed manual is basic and you'll want to spend time reviewing the online documentation. I'm still trying to figure out how to use the Sony FDRAX53/B and a "U-Stream" service to get a live stream going. There is a LOT of technology packed into this camcorder! Expect to spend some time reviewing it all. As I mentioned, Sony packed a TON of features in this device, and there's a learning curve to really understand and appreciate them all.

If you're planning a vacation or expecting a newborn child, BUY THIS CAMCORDER! You cannot take enough videos and photos of your kids when they're young, and the same goes for vacations -- this camcorder is small enough to tote with you (it does not like fog or water, though!) and the QUALITY of the images are incredible! It's not so heavy that it's going to be a burden.

The sound is very good, and there's a "gun" style microphone if you want to A) avoid wind noise B) capture audio of what you're shooting (like at a kid's soccer game) rather than local chitchat.

One thing that occurred to me while I was fiddling with the camcorder in my right hand, that being that if you were holding one of your kids in your left hand and the camcorder in your right hand and they both began to slip... which would you grab? This camcorder is THAT nice. Between the quality of the camcorder and its fantastic lens and the Sony software for image management and manipulation, this could be a major hobby in and of itself. You can easily edit, trim and combine videos with sound and add captions and text. For a consumer level product, the video and image editing suite is quite impressive. You will want a fairly modern computer, as I mentioned.

Something I come back to again and again as I figure the FDRAX53/B out is the absolute wonder of it. The small size, the quality of images, the ease of operation -- I just can't get over it. Beyond sensational and well into the realm of magical. I've never seen anything like the FDRAX53/B before.
text_fidelity_b: Sony FDRAX53/B 4K HD Video Recording Camcorder (Black)

Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Black Three things have changed my life! FITBIT, Walking Workouts and Walking 4 Fun.

FITBIT ONE - I have been faithfully wearing it. Using the calories in and out featured on the app. It has a safety leash and I wear it attached to my bra. I do a Jessica Smith DVD - 10K Walking Workout (see link on bottom of this review) and Leslie Sansone ("Walk at Home"). However, ONE is super accurate on my walks outside and around the office. My bottom line is 10K steps a day but I tend to walk 17K a day. I worked my way up to this since October 2015. I have a sedentary job so walking happens 3 to 4 times a day with a minimum of a mile on each walk. Yes, I have lost weight, @ 40 lbs. There is at least that much more that needs to be lost as well. Hair color is silver if that helps you define the situation.

I love the little activity record feature and use it often (hold down the button to start and hold it down to end when activity is over). This is great when competing with friends where a challenge is inevitable. Speaking of friends. YEAH! That is where the FITBITs excel. I have a few friends in my community now and I love keeping up with them. Motivation features are fantastic!

This little baby doesn't buzz, which also means that the battery life is HUGE!! I think it goes 7 to 8 days before I need to be charged up. I tend to let it go dead because it warns you it needs to be charged about 1 1/2 days before it really does. I've only charged mine 3x now. It takes about an hour to charge. I wait until the visible battery = FULL!

This sweet little tracker is awesome! I started test driving the flex before getting the ONE which I also enjoyed but not as much as this one. I will buy the HR when this ONE dies or I just feel like bringing home another one. The reason I like this one better than the flex is because I don't tend to be an arm swinger and for me this one seems to work better (walking while pushing a cart). The best thing about the arm band models is that you affix it and forget it (until charging time) for which you should get a phone alert.

I don't bother with the sleep feature because I have an app (Sleep Cycle Alarm) on the phone that I use for which I love the beautiful melodious wake up sound. However the ONE comes with a little band for you to slide the ONE into obtain the reading for sleep.

[[ASIN:B0070ZY80Q Eastvita Safety Leash for Pedometer - 6 units. Help Prevent Pedometor loss]]
[[ASIN:B00W85TAHE 10,000 Steps Weight Loss - Walk On: 5 Fat Burning Miles Walking Exercise DVD]]
[[ASIN:B00D2UMHWO Leslie Sansone: Walk It Off in 30 Days]]
This is my plan B when the ONE is charging. [[ASIN:B007ZWIJR2 Omron HJ-321 Tri-Axis Alvita Pedometer, Black]] This also picks up missed steps during DVD workouts.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit One Wireless Activity Plus Sleep Tracker, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Tripp Lite 900VA UPS Desktop Battery Back Up, 12 Outlet, 480W 120V Standby, Ultra-Compact, USB (INTERNET900U) First off, this was purchased for a 27" iMac for home usage.

I changed my previous configuration where my modem, router, NAS and iMac were all located in or on my office desk. These were all connected to a CyberPower CP1000PFCLCD that's been working perfectly for almost 5 years. After moving the location of the modem, router and NAS to a more central location; I moved the CyberPower UPS along with them. This left me for a need for a small UPS for the iMac only.

I originally looked at the smaller Cyberpower UPSs but then looked at the competition. The two I had narrowed it down to were similar in price, but the Tripp Lite offered a larger battery capacity. I then looked at their listings and found the Origin listed under the Product Information. The Tripp LIte stated that it was Made in USA or Imported while the Cyberpower was listed with a China origin. A little more searching and Tripp Lite is based out of Chicago. This essentially sealed the deal and the INTERNET 550U was ordered from Amazon.

Much to my disappointment, there was a large label on the side of the box clearly stating MADE IN CHINA. -1 Star

From the Manufacturer section of the listing would have you believe that the PowerAlert Software will work on the Mac OSX. After trying to find the PowerAlert Software from the Trip Lite web site would state the following...

"If you are a home or small office user, PowerAlert Local is for you. It allows you to monitor and control a UPS system connected to your computer through a USB or serial cable. It also supports automatic file saves and unattended computer shutdown during power outages."

Looking below this statement and there is no download availability for Mac OSX. The only Mac OSX software availability is called PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent and it states the following...

"If you need to automate computer shutdown during an outage without a USB or serial connection to a UPS system, or if you can’t use Java, PowerAlert Network Shutdown Agent is for you. When it detects a user-selected event (such as low battery) broadcast by a network-connected UPS system, it initiates shutdown or hibernation after a user-defined delay."

Not quite what I was looking for but I did find that the native software within Mac OSX seems to do what I need it to do without the need of installing additional software. -0 Stars

This UPS is considerably light compared to the larger CyberPower. For whatever reason, I was expecting something heavier. It gives the impression that it's cheap in feel. Not necessarily of any fault of the device but some perceived notion that I had. But when coupled with the horrible, plastic smell; it comes off as another characteristic of a cheap, Chinese product. -1 Star

In summary, we had a long power outage last weekend while I was at the computer. The UPS worked as it should, allowing me to shut down the computer.
text_fidelity_b: Tripp Lite 900VA UPS Desktop Battery Back Up, 12 Outlet, 480W 120V Standby, Ultra-Compact, USB (INTERNET900U)

text_fidelity_a:
Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter Shooting video outdoors with a DSLR requires, obviously, proper exposure. When shooting at 24 (23.978) frames per second, the normal shutter speed should be 1/50th of a second (1/60 at 29.97 fps). If the camera is set at the lowest ISO rating of 100, in bright daylight the f/stop would be around f/22. If you want to operate at wider aperture to achieve shallow depth of field, you need to cut the light.

This variable density filter allows such an adjustment. The problem is that it cuts the light by rotating two polarizing filters against each other. Polarizers can be tricky and, by design, modify the quality of light. Thus it may act unexpectedly.

One downside is that the front of the filter is not threaded and my 77mm model is a larger diameter than the 70-200mm Nikon zoom it fits on. So now the bayonet lens hood won't fit. Now I'm outdoors with a filter on the lens and no hood to block flare. There aren't any hoods that naturally fit the filter so you need to tape a hood to the outer ring or use a matte box.
text_fidelity_b: Tiffen 82VND 82 Millimeter Variable ND Filter

Xit XTETS Auto Focus Macro Extension Tube Set for Sony SLR Cameras (Black) UPDATE: I have since bought a couple of other cheap extension tube sets that looked similar. As it turns out, this set is actually very good for a crappy tube set. They all seem to cheap out on the electrical connections, so, especially when you're linking more than one tube, they can loose the auto signals and the camera may give you an error. But these work enough of the time to be useful. ALSO IMPORTANT: These are better for internal reflections than most. They have nice masks (baffles) in the tubes and have shiny bits hidden. That's crucial for good macro. Otherwise you will have hazy photos. SO I UPGRADED the rating from my original review below.
NOT ALL OF THESE TUBES THAT LOOK SIMILAR ARE THE SAME!

If you're using these for professional work, buy Canon tubes (or Kenko are supposed to be good).

ORIGINAL REVIEW
These tubes are sold under many names (The flippy metal release tabs and the smallest tube being 13mm instead of 12mm are a tip off).

I didn't really think the quality of extension tubes mattered. They're hollow tubes with some wires running through them for electrical contacts! Hard to mess up. But this set (at least the one I received) is messed up.

Sometimes my camera (Canon 70D) will just throw up an error when these are attached. Often just after snapping the shutter.

NEVER did autofocus work.

NEVER would more than one tube hold on to the connection to the camera long enough to give an exposure without an error.

I did manage to get some photos with auto exposure working, but always with manual focus. I don't think the image stabilizer was working either (from all the shaking). I didn't test it by switching it off.

The mounts are plastic, but not the kind you get on a cheap lens. More like the kind you get on a cheap kids toy with fake chrome. NOT smooth. You get a sort of sandpapery feel when you turn it into the mount.

I'm throwing mine away. I won't pay up for Canon's tubes (at that price - I'd buy the macro lens first), but there has to be something better than this.
text_fidelity_b: Xit XTETS Auto Focus Macro Extension Tube Set for Sony SLR Cameras (Black)

But I figured it's only $5, so it's worth a shot.

They arrived this morning and all I can think of is that whoever thought these were too tight or too small wasn't putting them on correctly. Maybe they thought they were just push-on instead of realizing that they have a flap (just like the ones that come with the headset) that needs to be lifted to go over the plastic part of the earpiece. That's what actually holds these things in place, people - otherwise they'd just fall off! Or maybe people aren't actually matching up the shape correctly. Either way - if you install them CORRECTLY, they fit perfectly.

These things are the correct size and I took some photos to compare the old Logitech-made pads with these. I also measured separately and they are the exact same size. If you take the time to look at how the original ear pads come off, you'll know exactly how to put these replacements on, and it'll take you all of about 10-15 seconds per ear pad.

These are virtually indistinguishable from the originals. I put these on and at first they seemed a little firmer than the original ear pads. However, I actually have a total of three G930 headsets (different purposes), so I was able to compare the feel of these ear pads to the original ear pads on one of the lesser-used, newer headsets. Again, pretty much identical - I guess they just get softer with use. Still, they are very comfortable even in their brand-new state, and I'm happy not to finish the day with black flakes on the sides of my face again.

PHOTOS:
I have three photos, two that are just comparing the back and front of the old pad to the replacement pad (and showing where the flap is that some people are apparently missing). The third photo is just showing the headset with one pad replaced so you can actually see that it looks pretty much the same as the original when installed correctly on the headset.

PALOVUE Lightning Earphones with Mircrophone Headphones Earbuds for Sports Workout MFi Certified Noise Isolation Compatible iPhone 14 13 12 11 Pro Max iPhone X XS Max XR iPhone 8 P 7 P NeoFlow Black While I tend to use wireless headphones most of the time, there are times, such as when flying that I need wired headphones and these are AWESOME.

These headphones are equipped with an iPhone Lightning Connector which is the perfect size to fit through the opening in the case on my iPhone, it snaps into place without issue and provides a stable connection.

The set comes with the headphones, a rubber squeeze case, 3 sets of silicone ear bud tips, 3 sets of silicone ear bud wings, and a wire clip.

I found that the preinstalled tips and wings (medium) fit perfectly for me.

The sound from these headphones is excellent - from the rich bass notes to the vibrant midtones to the bright treble. I tested these headphones with a wide range of audio - from audiobooks to jazz, heavy metal, country, classical and blues - everything sounded amazing.

The noise cancelling feature works really well on these headphones. Noise cancelling is a complex process where a processor must detect ambient noise, both frequency and amplitude, through the microphone and then “block it” by creating an exactly opposite noise thus cancelling out the ambient noise. Some noises are more easily cancelled than others and some processors within headphones do a better job at cancelling than others. I have to say I am thoroughly impressed with the noise cancelling these headphones achieve.

The microphone picks up perfectly on calls in my tests the other person had no issues hearing me crystal clear.

The control module allows you to easily increase or decrease the volume. Start / stop / pause music or answer / end calls.

These are a great set of wired headphones that performed very well in all of my tests. This is definitely a product I would recommend.

OTTERBOX DEFENDER SERIES Case for iPad mini (5th Gen ONLY) - Retail Packaging - BLACK So. Yes. It’s sturdy and seems it’ll protect an iPad really well.

Unfortunately, for the past 6 years, we’ve been spoiled by an iPad mini case made by Ballistic, that isn’t made any more. So I just don’t buy “well sure it’s inconvenient and bulky but it has to be, to protect well.” It really does not.

This plastic Otterbox uses is so very rigid, the protective cover is extremely difficult to pop on and off. When kiddo’s alarm goes off and he’s already off somewhere, it takes me ages to get the thing open to shut it down. I also can’t find the power or volume buttons easily by touch, they blend in so much.

What’s outright laughable is the kickstand. It’s on the inside of the cover that you take off, so you set the iPad on it. It doesn’t sit very securely at all, and now that this model has the pencil holder, in some positions it won’t stay up - it teeter totters right over! So no, it’s not a 4 position kickstand, but a 3 position. The whole situation is anything but stable, so if there’s a tug on a charger or headphone cord, instead of just sliding a tiny bit on the table or not doing anything at all, it slips off the kickstand and ... well, this is how we already know it’s sturdy, as the thing ended up on the floor more times in the first day than the iPad did in a year in its old case.

It’s quite heavy compared to other choices that offer similar protection, and very very difficult to install. I am never need to read directions type, and these directions were meaningless. It required a YouTube and a lot of swearing, plus a sliced open cuticle, to get it on. Even then it didn’t seat properly around the speakers and needed quite a bit of poking into place with a toothpick.

I sincerely hope there will be a day when there’s another rugged iPad mini case, with a kickstand and a shell that goes over the screen. Because this just doesn’t cut it.

Inventiv Sport Wireless Bluetooth Audio Sunglasses, Open Ear Headphones Music & Hands-Free Calling, for Men & Women, Polarized Glasses Lenses (Black Frame/Blue Tint) I like to listen to audio books as I go on bike rides, so I've been looking for a product like this. When I run I use over the ear headphones, but I can't fit those on over or under my cycling helmet. These sunglasses are a great solution. There are speakers underneath the arms that broadcast music almost directly into your ears. The effect is an open ear speaker system that allows you to hear your music, but also lets you stay mindful of ambient noises.

The sunglasses have enough of a tint to be comfortable, but not so much that they are impractical in low light. The arms rest easily on your ears and the nose piece is a solid bit of plastic that does not pinch the bridge of your nose. The glasses are very light even with the battery and speaker system.

The sunglasses connect to your cell phone via Bluetooth without any issues. There is a large power button on the right arm that is easy to locate by touch. I preferred these for comfort and for sound quality to ear buds. The sound quality is about what you'd expect for tiny speakers mounted to the arms of sunglasses. It's not concert hall quality, but it gets the job done, and it's better than a lot of other speakers on the market.

These sunglasses are great for athletes who like to listen to music while they're out exercising. Also included is a case, a bag, a lens cloth, and a charging cable.
text_fidelity_b: Inventiv Sport Wireless Bluetooth Audio Sunglasses, Open Ear Headphones Music & Hands-Free Calling, for Men & Women, Polarized Glasses Lenses (Black Frame/Blue Tint)

Camera for Kids, 2.7K 48MP Digital Camera for Teen Boy and Girl with 32GB SD Card 16X Zoom, Compact Portable Mini Toys Cameras Christmas Birthday Festival Gift for 4-15 Year Old Kid Children (Green) Sadly, the point-and-shoot camera market has been cannibalized by phones, so you can't really find simple cameras like this from big brands anymore. Real point and shoot cameras were great because unlike phones, you get a zoom lens and real camera controls. This isn't that.
Additionally, this is NOT going to compete with a modern cell phone camera. It's about on par with a low end entry level cell phone, the kind that you can usually get for free with a contract (maybe barely a mid range and DEFINITELY not a flagship). It does NOT zoom, there is a digital zoom only. The good news is that it comes with a decent sized memory card and two batteries, so you can have a spare one ready to go. I wish it came with a battery charger so you can keep one on tap (the only way to charge the battery is IN the camera, which means you can't charge one while using the other sadly), but the fact you get a backup is nice at least.
The pictures aren't great, but they're fun for a kid to run around with. I can see an elementary school aged kid having fun with this, my 5 and 10 year old like it well enough. The item suggests "4-15 year old" and to be honest, I can NOT see a 15 year old enjoying this AT ALL. My 12 year old has a similar camera that is waterproof so at least she can say it's fun to use in the pool (which she does), but this kind of underwhelmed me for the asking price.

I used these for air travel and they worked great. I changed my rating to five stars. These worked perfectly for canceling out the drone of the engine so I could easily hear movies or books on my iPad. The even helped to tone down the ear piercing screams of the child who cried nonstop for the ten hour flight. I'm so happy with these. For the price they are just outstanding.
